text:
Don't Trust Anyone Who's Not Laughing

Be suspicious of gurus who never giggle. Watch out for spiritual teachers who speak in hushed, reverent tones about every single thing and look like they're perpetually attending a funeral for someone they didn't know very well. The divine is not that serious. It can't be. Because the divine is playing every role in the cosmic drama simultaneously—the hero and the villain, the genius and the fool, the saint and the screw-up—and only someone with an exquisite sense of humor would take on a project like that.

Think about it. If you were the infinite, eternal, boundless source of all existence, and you decided to manifest as a primate on a spinning rock hurtling through space, worrying about your tax returns and whether you said the wrong thing at a dinner party three years ago... wouldn't you find that hilarious? Wouldn't you be laughing constantly? Wouldn't the absurdity of it all be the most delicious thing you'd ever tasted?

The people who take themselves too seriously have forgotten they're wearing a costume. They've mistaken the mask for the face. They think they're important in a way that's heavy and rigid and separate. But the real mystics—the ones who've actually glimpsed behind the curtain—they're always laughing. Not in a condescending way. In a way that says, "Can you believe this? Can you believe we get to be here, doing this, feeling all of this? What a strange and beautiful thing."

So if someone tries to sell you enlightenment and they can't crack a joke, walk away. If someone claims to know the secrets of the universe and they've lost the ability to laugh at themselves, they're selling a cheap imitation. The real thing is light. The real thing is free. The real thing is the cosmic giggle that erupts when you realize you've been searching for what you already are.

Find people who laugh. Be one of them. That's the whole teaching. 🖤
